subject: general
question: Two taps can fill a cistern in 2 hours and 81 hours, respectively. A third tap can empty it in 81 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill the empty cistern, if all of the taps are opened together?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency of **Tap A** = 1/2 cistern/hr

Efficiency of **Tap B** = 1/81 cistern/hr

Efficiency of **Tap C** (Emptying) = −1/81 cistern/hr

Net Efficiency = (1/2) + (1/81) − (1/81) = 1/2 cistern/hr

Total time = 1 / (Net Efficiency) = 2 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 2 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling time **T₁** = 2 hrs, **T₂** = 81 hrs; Emptying time **T₃** = 81 hrs.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = **LCM** of individual times; Efficiency = **Work / Time**.

⇒ Total Efficiency = Efficiency(A) + Efficiency(B) + Efficiency(C)

⇒ Total Efficiency = 81 + 2 − 2 = 81 units/hr

⇒ Time taken = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 162 ÷ 81 = 2 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 2 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Efficiency

Filling pipes have **positive efficiency**, while emptying pipes (leakage) have **negative efficiency**.

Net Rate of Filling

If two pipes fill in x and y hours and one empties in z hours, Net rate = (1/x + 1/y − 1/z) per hour.

Total Work Concept

Total capacity is often assumed as the **LCM** of given time values for easier integer calculations.</p
